title: Audience component library
rule: EVERY audience surface builds from `@/iframe/audience` by default, and that default is ENFORCED (AHAM-867): a new / rebuilt slide that hand-rolls the tappable answer row instead of AnswerOptionList fails the build (the answer-option ratchet in audience-library-detector.mjs). The qualifier is PURPOSE, not taste — a slide with no answer options does not import AnswerOption; a slide that needs a tappable row does not hand-roll one.
why: The library is not a style preference, it is where six guarantees are implemented once: deck-tracking ink, the frosted surface that survives a photographic deck, the 44px touch floor, the submission lock across an iframe remount, host-delegated image upload, and the deck font on a `<button>`. A hand-rolled control re-opens all six, and every one of them has already cost this repo review rounds (AHA-136, AHA-148, AHAM-433).

sections.name: AnswerOptionList
sections.what: The whole answer block: rows, single or multiple selection, the 8px thumb-safety gap (fixed, no prop), optional live counts, and the quiz reveal.
sections.useWhen: A MULTIPLE-CHOICE question (trac nghiem): a fixed set of predefined answers the participant picks from — one of them, or several with `selection-mode="multiple"`. This is the default answer surface and covers nearly every quiz and poll; pass `options`, `v-model`, `ink` and `palette` and it carries the rest.
sections.notFor: Anything the participant composes or positions rather than picks: free text, a scale (ScaleSlider), a drawing, an image. Also not a set of filters or tags they toggle without submitting — short inline toggles are Chip.
sections.replaces: Replaces a hand-built tappable answer row — a tappable row carries the submission lock, the deck ink, the frosted surface and accent-by-position — hand-rolling the row re-opens all four

sections.name: AnswerOption
sections.what: One tappable answer row, driven entirely by a state object rather than by working its own state out.
sections.useWhen: The rare answer screen that is NOT a plain list — rows split across columns, interleaved with other content, or laid out on a board. Pair it with answerOptionState().
sections.notFor: An ordinary list of options. AnswerOptionList already repeats this and owns the gap, the selection mode and the counts; using the row directly means re-implementing those.
sections.note: The row itself, driven straight from answerOptionState(). Shown answered-and-revealed — the state with the most moving parts: a tick or cross on every row, the participant's own wrong pick carrying the incorrect tone, and the rows they did not pick muted.

sections.name: DraggableOptions
sections.what: A reorderable list — "put the options in the correct order". Each row wears the same frosted surface and ink edge as AnswerOption, plus a live ordinal badge; the participant reorders by dragging a row or with its up/down buttons. v-model is the ordered id array. An option's imageUrl is shown IN FULL (contain, never cropped).
sections.useWhen: The answer IS an ordering — ranking, sequencing, "sort these". The model you submit is the order itself, not a pick.
sections.notFor: Choosing option(s) from a set — that is AnswerOptionList (single or multiple). Ordering is a different answer shape, so a slide that only needs a pick does not reach for this.
sections.note: Drag a row with the grip, or reorder from the keyboard with the up/down buttons — the ordinal badges renumber live either way. Two options carry an image, shown in full (contained). v-model is the ordered id array.

sections.name: Input
sections.what: A single-line text field: the themed Ant `Input` (size large) with a FIXED white fill + Deep Space ink that does not track the deck, and an optional Ant `Form.Item` label above it that DOES track the deck ink.
sections.useWhen: The participant types one short line — a name, a word, a short answer. Pass `ink` (the deck's `slideProps.textColour`) so the label reads on a light deck and a dark one; the field stays white either way.
sections.notFor: A number (InputNumber, which adds steppers and a numeric model), a long free-text answer (TextArea), or a pick from a fixed set (Select / AnswerOptionList).
sections.replaces: Replaces a hand-built <input> — the themed Ant primitive gives a FIXED white fill + Deep Space ink, the optional deck-tracking Form.Item label, and the 56px/16px sizing with resting/hover/focus borders from `ahaSlidesAudienceTheme` — a hand-rolled single-line input re-opens all of that (wrong height, no deck-tracking label, contrast bugs).
sections.note: The themed single-line field — a FIXED white fill + Deep Space ink on any deck, with the label alone tracking the deck. Opt into the in-field counter with :show-count + :maxlength.

sections.what: A multi-line text field: the themed Ant `Input.TextArea` (size large) with a FIXED white fill + Deep Space ink that does not track the deck, and an optional Ant `Form.Item` label above it that DOES track the deck ink.

sections.what: A numeric field: the themed Ant `InputNumber` (size large) with up/down steppers, a numeric v-model, a FIXED white fill + Deep Space ink that does not track the deck, and an optional Ant `Form.Item` label above it that DOES track the deck ink.

sections.name: Select
sections.what: A dropdown: the themed Ant `Select` (size large) whose closed field has a FIXED white fill + Deep Space ink that does not track the deck, and an optional Ant `Form.Item` label above it that DOES track the deck ink.
sections.useWhen: The participant picks ONE value from a longer or space-constrained list where showing every option as a row would be too much — a country, a category, a long enumerated set. Pass `ink` (the deck's `slideProps.textColour`) so the label reads on any deck.
sections.notFor: A short set of predefined answers to a question — that is AnswerOptionList, which carries the 44px row target and the reveal states. Free text is Input / TextArea; a number is InputNumber.
sections.replaces: Replaces a hand-built <select> — the themed Ant primitive gives the dropdown-selector fill on `.ant-select-selector` as a FIXED white with Deep Space ink, the optional deck-tracking Form.Item label, and the 56px/16px sizing with resting/hover/focus borders from `ahaSlidesAudienceTheme` — a hand-rolled select re-opens all of that (wrong height, no deck-tracking label, contrast bugs).
sections.note: The themed dropdown — fixed white selector, deck-tracking label. Options come from the :options prop (a disabled option is shown); callers needing groups pass their own <SelectOption>s in the slot.

sections.name: Timer
sections.what: A countdown: a bar that drains as the time runs out, with the clock beside it. One CSS animation off an absolute `endsAt`, never a rAF loop.
sections.useWhen: The question is time-limited and the participant needs to see how long is left. Pass the host's absolute end instant, not a duration.
sections.notFor: A bare `(mm:ss)` badge with no bar — that is the native CountDownTimer shape and this library has no component for it; build the text and use formatClock(). Also not a progress bar for anything that is not time.
sections.replaces: Replaces a hand-built countdown — a countdown driven from a rAF loop or a per-tick counter drifts on a backgrounded tab and runs the compositor for the length of the question — Timer is one CSS animation off an absolute end instant

sections.name: ScaleSlider
sections.what: A rating scale: the themed Ant Slider with a label at each end and a live readout of the value under the thumb.
sections.useWhen: The participant rates one statement on a range. `accent` is REQUIRED and comes from the deck palette by position — see `scaleAccentRule`.
sections.notFor: A two-ended range selection, or a slider that sets a quantity rather than an opinion — those want the themed Ant Slider directly.
sections.replaces: Replaces input[type=range] — a raw range input carries none of the audience theme — the native scale needed ~150 lines of vendor-pseudo CSS to look like anything

sections.name: ImageUploader
sections.what: Attach a photo to an answer. The HOST performs the upload; this owns the frame, the busy and failed states, the preview and the remove.
sections.useWhen: The slide accepts a picture from the phone. Reach for the default `area` variant when uploading the image IS an important action in the slide type — the thing the participant came to do, or half of the answer — because the dropzone is a target sized to say so. Use the compact `button` variant when a photo is optional garnish beside a text answer, so it does not outweigh the field that actually carries the response. Declare `enableImageSubmissionSetting`, gate on `slideProps.imageSubmission`, and pass the host's `uploadImage()` through.
sections.notFor: A presenter-side image pick — that is the host's own `openUploadImageModal` crop flow, not this. And do not spend the `area` variant on an upload nobody is expected to use: a full dropzone on an optional photo reads as a required step and suppresses the text answer beside it.
sections.replaces: Replaces input[type=file] — the HOST performs the upload (uploadImage()); a file input or a FileReader means the slide is doing the host's job, and the signed-URL contract goes with it

  <!-- The HOST uploads. Pass its function through; never build a file input, and
       never hold the file yourself. -->
  <ImageUploader
    v-model="image"
    :upload-image="uploadImage"
    :ink="slide.textColour"
    @error="showToast"
  />

  <!-- compact variant, for beside a text field -->
  <ImageUploader v-model="image" variant="button" :upload-image="uploadImage" />
</template>

sections.name: SubmitButton
sections.what: The ONE primary submit CTA per audience screen, with the whole audience-CTA contract baked in (AHAM-874 folded the old AudienceSubmitButton in). Fill = the deck's first palette colour (`accent`) with a readable black/white label; a 10%-deck-ink hairline (`ink`); disabled = grey. Plus the close/lock/loading state machine — `submissionClosed` swaps the label for a lock glyph + a caption and drops the accent so the button goes grey-disabled, `loading` shows the spinner — and the font-inherit guardrail (`font-family: inherit` + a 48px touch floor + 600 weight) that makes the CTA track the deck font live, fixing the AntD ConfigProvider static-font bug. All baked in so the deck-fill, the edge, the grey-disabled, the closed state and the live font hold by construction rather than per slide.
sections.useWhen: The screen has a submit / lock-in / place-bid action. Pass `ink` (deck textColour) and `accent` (`presentationColorPalette[0]`); add `submission-closed` + `closed-label` when the host can close submissions, and `loading` while a submit is in flight. Never hand-roll `<a-button type="primary">` for the submit — that re-opens the fixed-purple / no-border / dimmed-disabled defects and the byte-identical `.submit-btn { min-height: 48px; font-family: inherit }` block copied across fill-in-the-blanks, two-by-two-grid-v2, draw-answer-v2 and budget-allocation-v2.
sections.notFor: A secondary or tertiary action (skip / change / back) or a destructive remove — those step DOWN from the primary. Two primaries on one screen means neither is the submit.
sections.note: The one primary action per screen. Its fill is the deck's first palette colour (:accent); the label is a readable black/white picked against that fill, never deck ink. Ant's grey handles the disabled state. The in-flight (loading) and closed/locked states are built in — closed drops the accent to Ant's grey and shows the lock caption when the host stops submissions.

sections.name: InstructionLine
sections.what: One centred instruction line — "Swipe a card, or tap a side", "Tap or swipe to answer". The DEFAULT audience body: 16px, regular (400), the deck's own text colour (AHAM-701 issue 2a). Deliberately UNBOXED: no card, pill, border or background, so the deck shows straight through.
sections.useWhen: The screen needs a hint about HOW to answer. Pass the deck ink; the line reads in it directly so it tracks a light deck and a dark one. EVERY slide's instruction goes through this one component — the reported defect was two slides styling the same line differently.
sections.notFor: Anything that is not an instruction — a result, a status, an error. Use a card or a semantic colour for those.
sections.replaces: Replaces a hand-styled idle hint — the default 16px regular deck-ink body is fixed here once; a hand-picked size/weight/grey drifts between slides and dies on one deck or the other
sections.note: The one fixed idle hint — 16px regular deck ink, centred — so a hand-picked size/weight/grey never drifts between slides.

sections.name: WaitingForHost
sections.what: The centred lobby / passive-phase screen: a pulsing icon, a headline and a muted helper line. Renders the SCREEN only — the gate is `useQuizReveal`'s `inLobby`, which this does not rebuild. Unboxed, deck-tracking ink, reduced-motion-safe pulse.
sections.useWhen: The audience must wait for the presenter to start (a quiz lobby, a not-yet-open round). Gate it with `v-if="inLobby"` and pass `ink`, `headline`, `subline`.
sections.notFor: The post-submit wait — that is SubmittedCard, which says the answer is locked. This is the BEFORE, when there is nothing to answer yet. It replaces a hand-built waiting screen, which re-opens the contrast question and usually hard-codes a grey sub-line.
sections.note: The lobby / between-rounds waiting screen. The whole screen derives from the deck ink; the icon, headline and subline are all overridable via slots.

sections.name: AudienceIdentityStrip
sections.what: The "Submitting as {emoji} {name}" header, with an optional uppercase eyebrow. Centralises the ONE anonymous rule (hide the emoji, fall the name back to "Guest") so it can't drift between slides. Unboxed — deck ink for the name, a muted mix of it for the eyebrow, nothing painted.
sections.useWhen: The phone should show WHO is answering above the answer surface. Pass `ink`, `name` (`audienceName`), `emoji` (`audienceEmoji`); the strip decides whether the emoji shows.
sections.notFor: Editing identity (that is the host's `updateAudienceData`), or any line that is not the participant header — an instruction is InstructionLine. It replaces a hand-built 'Submitting as {emoji} {name}' line, where every copy re-decided whether to show the emoji for an anonymous participant and re-picked the muted eyebrow grey.
sections.note: A compact 'Submitting as …' identity line for the screens that genuinely need it (an anonymous participant falls back to the guest name). It is NOT the default header — the audience app already shows who joined.

sections.name: Card
sections.what: A swipeable content card on the deck's own surface — the frosted wash plus an ink hairline, with the deliberate-travel threshold and the spring-back already in it.
sections.useWhen: The SWIPE-CARD shape: the participant is handed one thing at a time and throws it left or right to answer (this-or-that, would-you-rather, a sorting deck). That is what this is for, and the gesture is on by default because of it.
sections.notFor: A static panel. `swipeable="false"` exists for the odd card in a swipe deck that must not move, not as a way to get a generic box — if all you need is the frosted surface, call `audienceSurface()` / `audienceBorder()` and put them on your own element. And never wrap the whole audience screen: the screen is transparent over the deck by contract, so a card around everything paints a surface the deck did not ask for.
sections.replaces: Replaces Ant Card / a bespoke panel — Ant's Card paints its own opaque surface, which reads as a foreign block on a dark deck
sections.note: Swipeable by default — drag it sideways to see the gesture resolve.
